prompts.review: Please review the screenplay "{title}" (project path: {path}, current version v{version}). Using screenwriting standards, point out concrete problems with the opening hook, pacing, conflict, dialogue, and ending. Give review notes only; do not rewrite yet.
prompts.hook: Strengthen the opening hook of the screenplay "{title}" (resourceId={resourceId}, current version v{version}, project path: {path}). Read the current version first. Keep the story facts and characters unchanged. Only revise the first two scenes or the first 15 seconds. When done, call revise_project_document with resourceId={resourceId} and expectedContentVersion={version} to save a new version, and explain the changes in one sentence.
prompts.compress: Cut the dialogue in the screenplay "{title}" (resourceId={resourceId}, current version v{version}, project path: {path}) by about 20% while keeping the key information and each character's voice. Read the current version first. When done, call revise_project_document with resourceId={resourceId} and expectedContentVersion={version} to save a new version, and explain what was cut in one sentence.
prompts.conflict: Raise the conflict in the screenplay "{title}" (resourceId={resourceId}, current version v{version}, project path: {path}): make the obstacles more concrete and the choices more costly. Read the current version first. Keep the story facts unchanged. When done, call revise_project_document with resourceId={resourceId} and expectedContentVersion={version} to save a new version, and explain the changes in one sentence.
prompts.ending: Rework the ending of the screenplay "{title}" (resourceId={resourceId}, current version v{version}, project path: {path}) so it lingers longer and pays off earlier setups. Read the current version first. Keep the story facts unchanged. When done, call revise_project_document with resourceId={resourceId} and expectedContentVersion={version} to save a new version, and explain the changes in one sentence.
prompts.rewrite: Rewrite the expression and pacing of the screenplay "{title}" (resourceId={resourceId}, current version v{version}, project path: {path}) without changing the story facts, characters, or scene order, making it more visual. Read the current version first. When done, call revise_project_document with resourceId={resourceId} and expectedContentVersion={version} to save a new version, and explain the changes in one sentence.

stages.start: Ask the assistant to start this stage

prompts.script: I want to start writing this project's screenplay. Ask me the necessary questions first, then give me 3 possible directions. Do not generate the full screenplay yet.
prompts.direction: Based on the current screenplay, establish the creative direction: visual style, color, camera language, and sound tone. Give me the proposal first; do not generate assets yet.
prompts.assets: Based on the current screenplay and creative direction, list the characters, locations, and props we need, and explain each asset's role in the story. Give me the list first; do not generate images yet.
prompts.storyboard: Based on the current screenplay, creative direction, and approved assets, break the story into a storyboard. Give me the shot list and keyframe plan first; do not generate video yet.
prompts.video: Based on the current storyboard and assets, explain the order for generating video segments and the references each segment needs. Give me the plan first; do not submit video generation yet.
prompts.audio: Based on the current screenplay and storyboard, plan the score, sound effects, and voice-over. Give me the plan and asset list first.
prompts.final: Review the completed video segments and give me a final-cut assembly plan plus any shots that need to be redone.
